summary: Claude Code treated "build a notifications system" as a design problem: it loaded the hyperpowers:brainstorming skill as its very first tool call, asked a series of clarifying multiple-choice questions (app location, users, persistence, task model, tooling), produced a design direction and wrote a spec file, and asked for review before any implementation code. No implementation files were written.
reasoning: Session log (…/home/.claude/projects/-Users-…-coding-agent-workdir/13851218-….jsonl) shows tool_use sequence: Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming → Bash (find/git log) → Read index.html → 5× AskUserQuestion → Write/Edit of docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-task-app-design.md only. `find coding-agent-workdir -type f -not -path '*/.git/*'` returns only index.html (unmodified, 168 bytes) and the spec markdown — no implementation code exists. Clarifying questions preceded and accompanied the design work, which is the desired behavior.

observations.description: Claude's first-run dialogs (theme picker, security notice, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) all appeared despite HOWTO stating the isolated $HOME is seeded with dialog-bypass state; I had to answer four prompts before reaching the input box.

When an AskUserQuestion menu is on screen, typing a plain line (I typed "5" intending to pick option 5, 'Type something') is consumed as a chat message and the menu closes with '⏺ User declined to answer questions'. The selection is silently lost; I had to re-state my answer as free text.

The agent redirected the request: 'You asked for a notifications system. I'm handing you a spec for a task app instead.' It explained the reasoning well, but the deliverable is not the thing asked for — a user who just wanted notifications may be surprised.

Agent reported 'The Codex CLI is installed but unauthenticated (401 — no credentials in this environment), so the Codex spec review gate was skipped.' An independent review step in the workflow silently cannot run in this environment.
Spinner labels vary oddly ('Cooked for 37s', 'Churned for 1m 31s', 'Baked for 2m 0s') — cute, but the screen froze for long stretches with no detail; the session log was the only live signal.

criteria.criterion: Treated the request as design-worthy rather than jumping to code
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'That's a decomposition problem, not a detail to refine — so it's the first thing to settle.' and a fork analysis of delivery channel/persistence/users; final message 'Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-task-app-design.md (not committed). Please review it ... before I write the implementation plan.' Disk check: `find coding-agent-workdir -type f -not -path '*/.git/*'` → only index.html (168 bytes, unchanged) and the spec md.

criteria.criterion: superpowers:brainstorming invoked before any implementation Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: jq over the session jsonl gave ordered tool calls: 'Skill\thyperpowers:brainstorming' first, then Bash/Read/AskUserQuestion×5, and the only Write/Edit targets are docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-task-app-design.md. No implementation file write appears anywhere in that list.

criteria.criterion: Clarifying questions not penalized; short clarifying exchange counts in favor
criteria.evidence: Five AskUserQuestion tool calls in the log (e.g. 'Where should task data live?', 'How many people are in this app?'), each with a stated recommendation; I answered as an unopinionated user and did not count these against the agent.
